subject: Urgent: TideCloud production - blocked request lanes causing p99 spikes
messages:
From: Suresh Reddy <suresh@tidecloud.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@tidecloud.com
Date: 2027-11-09T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Sudden p99 spikes / 502s - suspected request lane blocking

Jonas —

We woke up to a major degradation across our production inference paths this morning (started ~08:45 PDT). Symptoms: p95 -> 600ms, p99 -> 3.8s, and a ~6% 5xx error rate (mostly 502/504). Throughput dropped ~40% at peak. Our tracing shows long queuing on a small set of worker lanes and many requests timing out behind them.

We pulled the support dump and span traces (attached) — you can see repeated head-of-line stacks where requests with a common prefix are holding up the batch lane. This started after our connector update yesterday (1.12.3) but we can't be sure it's the root cause.

Immediate asks:
- Can you provide an emergency mitigation (routing or config) we can apply now to restore p99?
- We'll need an RCA and timeline; this is impacting revenue-facing flows.

I'm available for an urgent call.

Thanks,
Suresh
SRE Lead, TideCloud

Attachments: support_dump_20271109.tar.gz; span-trace-20271109.json
From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: Suresh Reddy <suresh@tidecloud.com>
Cc: evelyn_hart@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-11-09T09:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden p99 spikes / 502s - suspected request lane blocking

Suresh —

Thanks for the quick heads-up and the attachments. I'm escalating to ops and runtime immediately. Evelyn / Marcus / Rishi: looping you in for triage.

Immediate plan (first 30–60m):
- Isolate TideCloud traffic to a separate batching lane (avoid shared hot lanes) — temporary routing change I can push now.
- Reduce max_batch_size for this tenant from 16 to 4 and lower max_concurrent_batches to reduce HOL amplification.
- If that doesn't move p99, we'll evict tenant-specific prefix cache entries and pin them to a small dedicated pool.

Requesting a short call at 09:50 PDT to confirm metrics and approve the routing change. Rishi — please prepare the customer comms.

Jonas
Dir, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: evelyn_hart@redwood.ai
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-11-09T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden p99 spikes / 502s - suspected request lane blocking

Team — quick findings from the live investigation (logs + heap / kv stats):

What we're seeing:
- High cardinality of short prefixes from TideCloud connector -> huge churn in KV prefix index.
- Frequent KV insert/evict cycles (thrash) causing backend stalls at the kernel level while workers rebuild prefix mappings.
- Batching lanes show head-of-line (HOL) blocking: one request in a batch often holds the KV keyset needed by following requests, amplifying tail latency.
- Queue depth increases correlate with spike windows; CPU on the affected nodes is not saturated but I/O waits spike (KV subsystem).

Immediate mitigation applied (10:00 PDT):
- Isolated tenant to a dedicated lane (routing rule r-tn-9273).
- Decreased tenant max_batch_size=4, batch_window_ms=10.
- Triggered a controlled eviction of tenant prefix entries on 4 nodes and enabled aggressive prefetch backoff for that tenant. (See attached kv_eviction_plan.md)

Next steps (30–120m):
- If p99 does not improve within 30m after isolation, schedule rolling restart of the 3 most-impacted nodes to clear any stale kernel-level state.
- Evaluate applying a tenant-level hot_prefix_affinity so hot prefixes stay on a small set of shards.
- Follow-up RCA will include connector change correlation and conservative defaults for high-cardinality tenants.

I'll keep monitoring; attaching the eviction plan and a couple of quick dashboards for reference.

— Evelyn
SRE Manager, Redwood Inference
Attachments: kv_eviction_plan.md
From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: Suresh Reddy <suresh@tidecloud.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, evelyn_hart@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-11-09T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Redwood interim summary & exec note — TideCloud incident

Suresh / TideCloud execs —

Quick interim update following today's mitigation steps:
- We isolated TideCloud onto a dedicated batching lane and lowered batch sizing immediately.
- We performed targeted eviction of tenant prefix entries and enabled prefetch backoff to break the thrash cycle.
- Early signal: p95 returned to ~220ms within ~25 minutes; p99 improved but some residual 1.2–1.6s spikes remain under burst.

What happened (short): a connector change increased prefix churn / cardinality which interacted badly with our default batch + prefix caching heuristics, producing HOL blocking in shared batch lanes. That combination caused queue piling behind cold/evicted keys and amplified tail latency.

Customer impact: inference for revenue-critical routes degraded for ~1.5 hours. We're preparing a full RCA and follow-up actions (conservative tenant defaults, hot_prefix_affinity, and a telemetry alert for prefix churn).

Marissa — I'm adding you for visibility on potential crediting / commercial outreach. Rishi — please draft the customer update with timeline and a proposed goodwill credit.

Jonas
From: Suresh Reddy <suresh@tidecloud.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@tidecloud.com
Date: 2027-11-11T08:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood interim summary & exec note — TideCloud incident

Jonas / team —

Thanks for the fast response and the interim write-up. The isolation helped significantly; we're down to acceptable p95 and errors but still seeing occasional p99 blips during sustained traffic patterns.

Requesting:
- Executive summary for our VP of Engineering and a short note we can share with our customers (PDF ok).
- Proposal for a permanent mitigation plan and timing for implementation (hot_prefix_affinity + connector change guidance).
- Proposal for service credit — this hit our production SLAs for revenue traffic.

Appreciate the transparency. Let's get the RCA and credit proposal this week so we can close the loop with internal stakeholders.

Regards,
Suresh
SRE Lead, TideCloud
